title: The label question: which kind of record does each reference point to?
asOf: Worked example: a real decision explainer from 23 Sep 2026, 03:50 UTC · numbers are a snapshot of that analysis

intro.title: Which kind of record does each reference point to?
intro.sub: Click any box. Left column: where answers come from. Middle: the four groups of fields. Right: what the answer unblocks.
intro.proseHTML:
What a reference is. A PlanGraph record points at other records by a content ID, which is a fingerprint of the other record's bytes. The fingerprint is computed with a label in front, such as proposal or source record, so a proposal can never be passed off as a source record.

The gap. To check a reference, the code must know which label the field uses. The spec never says so for 141 fields. pg-core (the foundation that checks every record) therefore refuses those references, and records that contain them cannot be built.

What the evidence shows. The spec states the label for 3 fields. Its worked examples use one label consistently for about 115 more. For 12 fields the label depends on what the record carries. 14 fields have no example at all.

The plan now, after an independent review by a second agent on a different model. Write labels into the spec only where the evidence is strong: stated by the spec, or seen consistently in at least two independent example families. Everything weaker, including the 12 variable fields and the 14 with no example, stays as a clear refusal that names the field, until someone decides it. Nothing is guessed, and any entry can be changed later.

The numbers. Of 141 fields, 32 would become rules in the spec (5 stated or near-stated, 27 with strong evidence) and 109 would keep refusing by name (85 weak, 10 that vary, 14 with no example). That is deliberately cautious: it adds only what the evidence can carry.

What I need from you. Reply in chat: OK to proceed with this safer plan, or stop to leave the spec unchanged (pg-core keeps refusing those fields and this item stays open).

nodes.name: The spec text
nodes.does: The written rules in the spec. They name the label for only 3 of the 141 fields.
nodes.built: Normative: whatever it says is binding.

nodes.name: The spec worked examples
nodes.does: Thousands of example records with exact expected fingerprints. Recomputing the fingerprints shows which label each field actually used.
nodes.built: Evidence, not law: almost all examples came from one generator, so a field seen only once or twice is weak evidence.

nodes.name: Independent second opinion
nodes.does: A second agent on a different model reviewed the plan and asked for it to be tiered: strong evidence becomes a rule, weak evidence stays a refusal.
nodes.built: Adopted before any change is committed.

nodes.name: 5 stated or near-stated
nodes.does: The spec text states the label, or states the rule the label follows (edges, file contents, fingerprints, signatures, and the check on typed references).
nodes.built: Written into the table as rules. Lowest risk.

nodes.name: 27 strong
nodes.does: At least three distinct examples, from at least two independent example families, all agreeing, with the matching authoring and final schemas in agreement.
nodes.built: Written into the table as rules. 27 of the roughly 115 fields that the examples settle meet this bar.

nodes.name: 85 weak
nodes.does: Seen in the examples but too thinly: one or two examples, or one example family only.
nodes.built: Recorded as provisional: pg-core still refuses them, with a message that names the field, until someone decides.

nodes.name: 10 vary
nodes.does: The label depends on what the record carries. The observed labels are listed for checking; building these records stays refused.
nodes.built: Not guessed. The allowed labels are listed for checking, and building such records stays refused until the spec states the rule.

nodes.name: 14 unknown
nodes.does: Nothing in the spec shows which label these use.
nodes.built: Stay refused, with a message that names the field.

nodes.name: pg-core reference check
nodes.does: The foundation that checks every incoming record. It needs the label to check a reference.
nodes.built: Can check every field with a rule; refuses the rest by name.

nodes.name: Typed records the other parts use
nodes.does: Ledger events, validated changes and other records built through pg-core.
nodes.built: Each record whose references all have rules becomes buildable. The analysis reports exactly which.

nodes.name: pg-ledger storage test
nodes.does: The end-to-end test of pg-ledger saving and loading through pg-core.
nodes.built: Runs if the records it needs become buildable; otherwise it stays skipped and this item stays open.

items.l: Refused until the spec states a rule
Depends on which records become buildable

EX-FB.title: Strong evidence
EX-FB.carries: Same label in every example, two or more example families.

EX-FC.title: Weak evidence
EX-FC.carries: One or two examples, or one family only.

EX-F12.title: Varies
EX-F12.carries: Different labels depending on the payload.

REV-FC.title: Keep weak ones refused
REV-FC.carries: The reviewer asked that weak evidence not become a rule.

REV-F12.title: No guessed rules
REV-F12.carries: The reviewer asked that no selection rule be guessed from examples.

FC-PGC.title: Refused by name
FC-PGC.carries: pg-core refuses and names the field.

F12-PGC.title: Refused by name
F12-PGC.carries: pg-core refuses and names the field.

F14-PGC.title: Refused by name
F14-PGC.carries: pg-core refuses and names the field.

PGC-REC.title: Builds records
PGC-REC.carries: Records whose references are all checkable can be built.

REC-LEDG.title: Enables the test
REC-LEDG.carries: pg-ledger storage runs if its records can be built.
